replacements.text: The delegation skill's routing table is meant to be the only inventory of model ids. Nothing enforced that. A new test suite reads the Markdown files under `src/`. It excludes files under an `evals` or `node_modules` directory. The suite fails `make ci` when a file names a model id the table does not list. Anthropic aliases such as `sonnet` are not caught.
The patterns are case-sensitive. The real tree of 94 files lints clean.
A pytest suite beside the delegation skill fails on an unlisted model id. It fails on a table row elsewhere that names any id. It also fails when the routing table changes shape.
Each vendor naming scheme has one case-sensitive pattern. A family name in prose is not an id.
The routing file's Providers table became a list. The lint allows two tables there.

The lint is a PEP 723 pytest suite. The content gate discovers it by its `*_test.py` name. The installer's ignore file already keeps such a file out of the deploy. Nothing here ships.

The suite reads every Markdown file under `src/`. It excludes paths under an `evals` or `node_modules` directory. It fails when a file names a model id absent from the routing table's models table. It fails when a table row outside the routing table names any model id. Such a table is a second inventory. It fails when the tier grid gains a column. It fails when the models table gains, drops or renames one. It fails when the routing file holds a third table. It fails when the routing table is absent or lists no model id.

The six patterns cover the Claude, GPT and Gemini schemes. They also cover the three OpenRouter schemes for Gemini, Kimi and GLM. An OpenRouter id needs its vendor prefix. A file name that holds a model family is not an id. The Anthropic aliases are ordinary words. No pattern reads them as ids.

The Providers table was a third table in the routing file. Each of its rows became one sentence with the same three facts. Every other line of the file is unchanged.

All 34 cases failed against a stub lint that returned no files and no violations. Every case passes at the head.
The spec defines ids by vendor naming scheme. An alias is not one.
A table row elsewhere that names a listed id fails. The same id in prose passes.

questions.question: Add a separate Heads-up row noting that Anthropic aliases such as `sonnet` are not caught.
